log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Provide a reference for the first 14 current ISO 3166-1 entries and their associated codes, subdivision links and independence status.","tasks":["Find an entry by its English name.","Read or compare its alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes.","Locate its ISO 3166-2 link and independence status."],"relations":["Each row describes one country or territory; its codes, subdivision link and status belong together.","The two alphabetic codes and the numeric code are parallel identifiers.","The ISO 3166-2 link incorporates the entry's alpha-2 code."],"roles":["The header names each field; the first column acts as the visual row label even though no row headers are declared.","The remaining columns contain compact identifiers, a reference link and a short categorical status.","All 14 body rows have the same structural role."],"keep_whole":["Country and territory names should retain whole words where space permits.","Alpha codes and three-digit numeric codes, including leading zeroes, must remain intact.","ISO 3166-2 references should ideally stay intact because they are identifiers.","Header words should remain whole where feasible."],"may_wrap":["Multiword names can wrap between words.","Headers can wrap between words and at natural punctuation; narrow fitted columns may force breaks within header words or references."],"same_scale":["Alpha-2 and alpha-3 columns should have similar widths because they hold parallel short codes.","Body rows share one visual hierarchy; the name column deserves more space because its entries are longer."],"h_vs_v":"A fitted table exposes all fields at once but forces awkward breaks, especially in headers and links, and increases row heights. Scrolling preserves identifiers and compact rows, but readers must move horizontally to see later fields and may lose the name from view."},"designs":[{"widths":[103,40,40,40,90,46],"strategy":"Fit all six columns within 359px, protecting body codes and most name words while accepting forced breaks in headers, links and potentially longer names."},{"widths":[150,70,70,82,155,112],"strategy":"Use a compact scrolling table that keeps names and subdivision references readable while wrapping the longer headers."},{"widths":[200,118,118,121,155,112],"strategy":"Use a spacious scrolling reference table with all headers and body entries on one line, favoring rapid scanning at the cost of more horizontal travel."}]}
